sentences.text: Harpagofututor was an extinct eel-like cartilaginous fish with an elongate body ranging from 8.6 to 17 cm in length.
It featured a long upper medial fin that lacked a spine.
The jaws held triangular tooth plates similar to those found in living chimaeras.
Its cephalic claspers were considerably longer than the skull and are unique to this genus.
Researchers believe these specialized structures were used during mating.
Complete specimens were found in the Bear Gulch Limestone of Montana, while an isolated tooth was discovered in Whitrope, Scotland.
The genus was first described in 1982 by the palaeontologist Richard Lund.
The animal likely used its tooth plates to crush prey.
Harpagofututor belongs to the family Chondrenchelyidae, a group of Holocephali closely related to modern chimaeras.
This fish lived during the Early Carboniferous period, specifically between 326.9 and 323.6 million years ago in the Serpukhovian stage.
